newsitem.title: USA: Orphan says Sucraid gets FDA priority.
newsitem.headline: Orphan says Sucraid gets FDA priority.

text.p: Orphan Medical Inc said the U.S. Food and Drug Administration has accepted for filing and granted a priority review classification to the company's new drug application, or NDA, for Sucraid oral solution.
Sucraid is an enzyme replacement therapy for use in the treatment of the genetic disease known as congenital sucrase-isomaltase deficiency, Orphan said.

The status given the NDA "would mean an FDA goal of reviewing the NDA within a six-month time frame from the May 7, 1997 date of FDA receipt. Only new drugs that represent a significant advance over available therapy are granted priority attention and resources by FDA," Orphan said.

Sucrase is an enzyme produced in the small intestine that is needed for digestion of sucrose, or table sugar. Symptoms of CSID include frequent watery diarrhea, chronic malabsorption, and failure to thrive in infants and toddlers.

"It is believed that many cases of CSID may be unreported due to the difficulties associated with diagnosing the disease and it remains undetermined how many patients exhibit significant symptoms and seek treatment, although the number may be small," Orphan said.
Sucraid has been demonstrated in two controlled prospective clinical trials to alleviate the symptoms of CSID, the company said.
Presently, the only specific treatment of CSID consists of a life-long adherence to a sucrose-free diet, which can be difficult due to the prevalence of sugar in the American diet, the company said.
